request: how does the k-means algorithm group points into clusters?

composition.story: K-means groups points by iteratively assigning each point to the nearest centroid and then recomputing the centroid locations until assignments stabilize.

aha.observation: Points switch cluster membership dynamically as the boundary moves.

states.label: Initialize
states.sentence: Place initial centroids randomly in the space.
states.why: Starting positions anchor the first distance computation.

states.label: Assign Points
states.sentence: Assign each point to the nearest centroid.
states.why: Minimizes within-cluster variance for current centers.

states.label: Update Centroids
states.sentence: Recalculate centroids as the mean of assigned points.
states.why: Shifts centers to the true geometric average.

states.label: Check Convergence
states.sentence: Repeat until no points change their cluster assignment.
states.why: Stops computation when a stable optimum is reached.
